content:
Facts: Heirs challenged donations made to co-heirs seeking reduction; donated property subject to collation obligation without exemption.
Legal Framework: Art. 737 Civil Code (collation); Art. 553-564 Civil Code (reduction); Art. 745-746 Civil Code (collation methods and calculation).
Interpretative Issues: Whether reduction action is admissible when donations were made to co-heirs subject to collation; how collation operates versus reduction; when donee may choose collation method.
Legal Principles: Reduction action against co-heir donee is inadmissible unless donee was exempted from collation, as collation mechanism alone suffices to enable each co-heir to obtain inheritance share without resorting to specific protection for legitimate portions. When property donated to co-heirs must be collated, donees may choose collation method under Art. 746 Civil Code: either returning property in kind or imputing its value to their share. For property subject to collation by imputation, civil fruits calculation differs: if restitution in kind, annual rental value from succession opening; if imputation, legal interest on sum corresponding to asset value at succession opening. Collation ensures balance among co-heirs by forming estate to be divided according to legitimate succession shares.
